stories.h: Obi says Kwankwasiyya sticks have never hurt anyone
stories.p: Peter Obi has defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement who carry sticks at campaign events, saying the sticks have never been used to harm anyone. His comments, reported by Punch on Wednesday, come as concern grows over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Edo police arrest four security corps operatives
stories.p: Police in Edo State have arrested four operatives of the Edo State Security Corps accused of leaking police movements to suspected cultists in Adolor, Benin City. Police said officers on an operation found that information about their movements was being passed on, and the suspected cultists escaped arrest. One operative was paraded.

stories.h: NRS calls for simpler tax rules for creative sector
stories.p: The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and more business-friendly tax rules for Nigeria's creative economy. The revenue agency said easier rules would help unlock investment in film, music and other creative industries. The call was reported by Vanguard and ThisDay on Wednesday.

stories.h: Nollywood veteran Pete Edochie dies at 79
stories.p: Veteran Nollywood actor and former broadcaster Pete Edochie has died aged 79. His eldest son, Leo Edochie, announced on Instagram that he died at 12:30am on Wednesday, November 25, in Enugu. Punch reports he had battled prostate cancer. His death comes months after his colleague Olu Jacobs died at 84.

stories.h: Petrol imports via Lagos ports fall 52% in November
stories.p: Imports of petrol (PMS) through Lagos ports fell by 52.23 per cent in November, according to a Vanguard report published on Wednesday. Crude oil and bulk wheat were among the leading commodities handled at the Lagos ports during the month, the report said.

stories.h: Israeli strikes kill seven in Gaza despite ceasefire
stories.p: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas's director of internal security, Palestinian officials told AFP. Israel's military said it had struck a senior Hamas member. The strikes came despite a ceasefire that has been in place since last year, according to the report carried by TVC News.

stories.h: FCMB Group pre-tax profit doubles to N272.8bn
stories.p: FCMB Group Plc made a pre-tax profit of N272.8 billion in the nine months to September 30, up 103% from N134.5 billion a year earlier. The bank credited better interest margins and a lower cost-to-income ratio. Its annualised return on average equity rose to 30.1% from 22.4%.

stories.h: Air Peace to start London–Owerri flights Dec 15
stories.p: Air Peace will begin direct flights between London and Owerri, Imo State, on December 15, Punch reports. The airline will fly from both Gatwick and Heathrow airports with Boeing 777 aircraft. The new route is meant to make travel easier for people travelling between the United Kingdom and the South-East.

stories.h: NNPC says no Duke Oil crude money is missing
stories.p: NNPC Limited has rejected reports that $2.04 billion from crude cargoes lifted by Duke Oil, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for. The company said the sum is the gross value of the cargoes, all transactions were reconciled, and every cargo under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase programme was fully accounted for.

stories.h: INEC awaits police files to prosecute poll violence
stories.p: INEC says it is waiting for police case files before it can prosecute people accused of campaign violence ahead of the 2027 elections. Under the Electoral Act, first offences can attract fines of up to N5 million or 12 months in prison for individuals, and up to N10 million for political parties.

stories.h: FIFA adds Atilola Bashiru to NFF committee
stories.p: FIFA on Tuesday named Atilola Shina Bashiru as an additional member of the Normalisation Committee running the Nigeria Football Federation. His appointment brings the committee's membership to six, ThisDay reports. The committee was set up by world football's governing body to manage the federation's affairs.

stories.h: Benue police arrest 26 suspects, rescue five
stories.p: The Benue State Police Command says it arrested 26 suspects, killed three suspected bandits and rescued five kidnapped people in separate security operations across the state. The command gave the figures on Tuesday, reported by The Sun. The police described the arrests and rescues as part of ongoing efforts against crime in the state.

stories.h: Saraki, Ahmed's Offa robbery arraignment moved
stories.p: A Kwara State High Court in Ilorin on Tuesday stopped the planned arraignment of former Senate President Bukola Saraki and former Kwara governor Abdulfatah Ahmed in the Offa robbery case. The court ruled that proceedings cannot begin until both men are properly served with the charges, and adjourned to December 3.

stories.h: Lagos brings back 20% Ounje Eko food discount
stories.p: The Lagos State Ministry of Agriculture and Food Systems has announced the return of its 'Ounje Eko' food discount, which lets residents buy food items at 20 per cent off. The scheme is resuming ahead of the Christmas and New Year season to ease the cost of food for families in Lagos.

stories.h: AIICO and Cornerstone Insurance propose merger
stories.p: AIICO Insurance Plc and Cornerstone Insurance Plc have proposed to merge into one company with combined shareholder funds of about N194 billion, ThisDay reports. Both firms are among the 50 primary insurance underwriters that passed the industry's recent recapitalisation exercise, according to the newspaper report.

stories.h: FG vows crackdown on fake seeds
stories.p: The Federal Government on Tuesday promised tougher enforcement against fake and substandard seeds, Punch reported. It also unveiled a National Seed Sector Roadmap for 2026 to 2031, which it says will attract investment and improve farmers' access to quality seeds as part of efforts to protect food security.

stories.h: INEC chairman warns against violent 2027 campaigns
stories.p: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan on Tuesday warned politicians not to turn the 2027 general elections into a battlefield, Punch reported. He pointed to rising cases of violence, thuggery and intimidation during the campaigns. Police chiefs have issued similar warnings this week after deadly attacks on party supporters.

stories.h: Immigration Service starts 48-hour visa processing
stories.p: The Nigeria Immigration Service has begun processing visas within 48 hours under new reforms, PM News reported on Tuesday. Comptroller-General Kemi Nanna Nandap said the changes replace a slow manual system and are meant to cut delays, improve transparency and strengthen national security.

stories.h: CAF to implement ruling restoring Senegal's AFCON title
stories.p: CAF said on Tuesday it respects the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling that restored Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions and will take steps to apply it. CAS overturned CAF's March decision that had handed Morocco the title after Senegal's players walked off. Morocco has rejected the verdict and plans legal action.

stories.h: GBV costs Nigeria $3bn a year, minister says
stories.p: Gender-based violence costs Nigeria about $3bn a year, around 1.5% of GDP, Women Affairs Minister Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim said in Abuja, Vanguard reported. More than 27,000 cases of sexual and gender-based violence have been documented, and ActionAid called for stronger enforcement of existing laws.

stories.h: Bayelsa begins mass burial after boat accident
stories.p: Bayelsa State began a mass burial in Yenagoa on Tuesday for victims of the boat accident involving mourners travelling to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw, Punch reported. The accident killed 29 people. Governor Douye Diri has ordered a probe, and the House of Representatives called for safer boats and compulsory life jackets.

stories.h: Northern states dissolve NNDC board
stories.p: The 19 northern states that jointly own the New Nigerian Development Company (NNDC) have dissolved its board of directors and will name a new one, Vanguard reported from Kaduna. The decision was taken by the secretaries to the 19 state governments as part of a plan to reposition the company.

stories.h: Police invite Omo-Agege, six others over Ughelli attack
stories.p: Police have invited Ovie Omo-Agege, a Delta local council chairman and five other people over an attack in Ughelli, Channels TV reported on Tuesday. Police said the invitations are meant to establish each person's level of involvement. The attack followed campaign violence in the state that police say left six people dead.

stories.h: DSS asks court to close Sowore's defence
stories.p: The DSS has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to close activist Omoyele Sowore's defence in his cyberbullying trial, Punch reported. The agency's lawyer cited at least 14 adjournments, relying on the Administration of Criminal Justice Act. Sowore pleaded not guilty to the two-count charge in January.

stories.h: 17 killed in Zamfara road crash, FRSC says
stories.p: Seventeen people died in a road crash in Zamfara State, the Federal Road Safety Corps said on Tuesday, according to PM News. FRSC Sector Commander Aliyu Maaji blamed the crash on wrongful overtaking and sympathised with the families of the dead and the state government.

stories.h: NAFDAC challenges Edo committee on fake products
stories.p: NAFDAC has challenged the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee's power to seize regulated products, seal shops, impose fines or declare goods counterfeit without its authorisation, Nairametrics and Tribune reported. The agency also said a QR code scan alone is not enough to declare a product fake.

stories.h: Katsina suspends Emir of Daura, orders probe
stories.p: Katsina State Government has suspended the official engagements and travels of the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and set up a committee to investigate a foreign tourist's allegation of sexual assault against him, Premium Times and Punch reported. Amnesty International had condemned reported threats against the tourist.

stories.h: National Assembly approves $20.5bn loan plan
stories.p: The Senate on Tuesday approved President Bola Tinubu's external borrowing plan of $20.517bn and €1.45bn for projects in 2026 and 2027, after the House of Representatives had already backed it. Senators acted on the report of their Committee on Local and Foreign Loans, hours before Tinubu sought a revised 2026 budget.

stories.h: Tinubu unveils models of new Nigerian satellites
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday unveiled models of Nigeria's new optical and radar satellites at an event in Abuja, Punch reported. According to the report, the satellites are intended to strengthen national security, improve environmental monitoring and help grow the country's space economy. Further details of the programme were not yet available.

stories.h: Naira falls to eight-month low despite CBN sales
stories.p: The naira weakened 2.5% to N1,394 per dollar at the official market last Friday, its lowest in eight months, according to FMDQ data cited by Legit.ng. Weekly forex turnover rose 36.6% to $4.67bn even though the CBN sold about $1.30bn. Gross reserves dipped to $54.65bn. Analysts blamed investor demand and festive imports.

stories.h: NDC boycotts IGP's security meeting with parties
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress said it would boycott the Inspector-General of Police's security meeting with political parties on Tuesday. The party accused the police of failing to protect its members from attacks it blamed on ruling APC thugs, saying it would not lend legitimacy to the process. The APC's response was not included in the report.

stories.h: Delta rally violence: police confirm six dead
stories.p: Police have confirmed that six people died in violence at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State, on Monday. IGP Olatunji Disu ordered an impartial investigation, while Governor Sheriff Oborevwori visited the community on Tuesday and promised that those responsible would face justice.

stories.h: CBN keeps benchmark interest rate at 23%
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria kept its Monetary Policy Rate at 23% after its 308th MPC meeting in Abuja, Governor Olayemi Cardoso announced on Tuesday. He pointed to five straight months of falling inflation, now 14.06% in October. Cash reserve ratios stay at 45% for commercial banks and 16% for merchant banks.

stories.h: Defence chief warns media over military operations
stories.p: Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Olufemi Oluyede on Tuesday urged journalists not to reveal troop movements, operational locations or military capabilities, saying such reports can endanger soldiers. Speaking at a Defence Headquarters communication workshop in Abuja, he also warned about old videos and AI-made fake content and urged checks before publishing.

stories.h: Tinubu asks Reps to approve revised federal laws
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve the revised Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025 edition. In a letter read by the Speaker on Tuesday, he said the review removes 268 obsolete laws and keeps 664 principal enactments, along with 731 pieces of subsidiary legislation.

stories.h: Tinubu proposes N3.15tn cut to 2026 budget
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to cut the 2026 federal budget by N3.15 trillion, from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion, while keeping the N31.46 trillion deficit. He sent a bill to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, with a revised fiscal framework for the year.

stories.h: Plateau governor says state police will tackle insecurity
stories.p: Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang says a well-structured state police would help address insecurity in the state. He spoke in Jos while receiving the preliminary report of the advisory committee on state policing.

stories.h: Lagos Assembly advances new tenancy bill
stories.p: The Lagos State House of Assembly on Tuesday adopted its Housing Committee's report on the Lagos State Tenancy Bill, 2025. The bill would set out the rights and duties of landlords and tenants and the procedure for recovering premises. Committee chair Olusegun Ege presented the report, with Speaker Mudashiru Obasa presiding.

stories.h: Sanwo-Olu to open Ijegun-Ijagemo Road Wednesday
stories.p: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu will commission the newly completed Ijegun-Ijagemo Road on Wednesday, November 25, according to a state government statement reported by Business Post and PM News. Community members and senior officials are expected at the handover, and the government says the road should ease movement in the area.

stories.h: France and Nigeria sign three agribusiness agreements
stories.p: France and Nigeria have signed three agribusiness agreements and set out an energy roadmap at French Week 2026 in Lagos, organised by the FNCCI. The event also hosted a French Tech Summit, where French investors and Nigerian startups discussed areas where they could work together.

stories.h: Court voids Omo-Agege's NDC Delta Central ticket
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Warri on Tuesday nullified former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege's nomination as NDC candidate for Delta Central in 2027. The judge ordered INEC to remove his name, ruling the party had not filed a valid membership register before its primary. The suit was filed by Prof. Alexander Akpodiete.

stories.h: Morocco accuses Senegal FA chief in AFCON row
stories.p: Morocco's football federation has alleged that Senegal FA president Abdoulaye Fall phoned an arbitrator at the Court of Arbitration for Sport handling the disputed 2025 AFCON final. Senegal denies the claim. CAS was expected to give its ruling on Tuesday, though reports said Morocco's objection could delay it.

stories.h: EU launches fund for women facing poll violence
stories.p: Team Europe on Tuesday launched a €100,000 (about N152.9 million) rapid response fund in Abuja for women threatened by election-related violence before the 2027 polls. Running until March 2027, it covers medical, legal, counselling, safe housing and transport help. Organisers said it cannot be used for campaign funding.

stories.h: IGP Disu warns parties against campaign violence
stories.p: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu on Tuesday warned political parties, candidates and supporters against sponsoring violence, hiring thugs or using weapons to intimidate opponents ahead of the 2027 elections. Speaking at a high-level security meeting, he said no one is above the law and promised the police would stay neutral and professional.

stories.h: Ex-CJN Ariwoola warns against post-election violence in 2027
stories.p: Former Chief Justice of Nigeria Olukayode Ariwoola has warned against a repeat of the killings that followed the 2011 elections. He urged action to curb political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: WHO: Ebola responders trapped in DR Congo by fighting
stories.p: The World Health Organization says Ebola responders are trapped in the Democratic Republic of Congo because of heavy fighting. The WHO blamed the country's failure to contain the virus on insecurity.

stories.h: Lagos residents can now report poor artisan services
stories.p: The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) says residents with problems with tailors, plumbers, electricians, mechanics, carpenters, painters or air-conditioner repairers can report them. The agency offers complaint channels and mediation, especially where artisans delay jobs or abandon work after being paid.

stories.h: Indonesia factory fire death toll rises to 26
stories.p: Police in Indonesia say 26 people have now died in a fire at a factory, and another 28 people remain unaccounted for. Officials said an investigation has been opened into what caused the blaze. Rescue and search efforts were continuing at the site, Channels Television reported on Tuesday.

stories.h: US adds 24 Nigerians to deportation list
stories.p: The United States Department of Homeland Security has added 24 more Nigerians to its 'Worst of the Worst' list of foreign nationals facing removal from the country. Several Nigerian outlets reported on Tuesday that the new names bring the total number of Nigerians on the list to 157.

stories.h: Lagos Assembly backs raising magistrates' retirement age to 65
stories.p: The Lagos State House of Assembly has adopted a committee report on amending the Magistrates' Courts Law, 2015, which proposes raising magistrates' retirement age to 65. The report, adopted at Monday's plenary, aims to strengthen the magistracy and improve the administration of justice in the state.

stories.h: INEC to test BVAS in nationwide mock accreditation on Saturday
stories.p: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will hold a nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise with BVAS machines on Saturday, November 28, in selected polling units, including 490 in Lagos State. INEC has published the list of polling units and the hours as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Benue police arrest two suspects linked to Abuja robbery
stories.p: The Benue State Police Command says it has arrested two suspected members of an interstate robbery gang and recovered a stolen Camry car. Police linked the suspects to a robbery in Wuse 2, Abuja. Punch reports that one suspect later died after fleeing and being rearrested.

stories.h: 4,000 flood-hit Ogun farmers get farm support
stories.p: The National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) has given emergency support to 4,000 smallholder farmers in Ogun State whose farms were damaged by this year's rainy-season floods. The 2,800 rice farmers and 1,200 maize farmers are receiving fertilisers, herbicides and pesticides to help them recover.

stories.h: Infantino says Nigeria is not ready to host a World Cup
stories.p: FIFA President Gianni Infantino says Nigeria is not yet equipped to host the FIFA World Cup, pointing to gaps in stadiums, airports and transport networks. He gave the assessment in an interview with ARISE News in Abuja on Monday, when asked whether the country could host the tournament.

stories.h: Court freezes N135.5bn held by Nigerian Governors' Forum
stories.p: An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on about N135.5 billion (around $100m) held by the Nigerian Governors' Forum in a dispute over Paris Club refunds. The order stops the forum's trustees from withdrawing, moving or otherwise dealing with the money.
